The poller half collides with pinned pr-upkeep stage/replay invariants that t31 rewrites anyway, and the renames are only safe once no graph workflow listens for the old names (t37). deviations.what: Add task t38, engine wiring, before t32: run the declaration engine in the server, drive ExpireDue / EmitActionResults / DrainSubject / ThawAndReplay on a schedule, a switch-flip route using FreezeHook and ThawAndReplay, the t27 engine-side stamping refusal, the t10xt12 drain-on-close seam, and register the engine_declaration_engine identity
deviations.reason: No plan task owned wiring the declaration engine into a running binary. t9-t18 each built primitives and left explicit wiring obligations. t32 (shadow parity on real traffic) and t36 (live signals) cannot run without it. Owner approved.

deviations.what: Add task t38c and a code.result trigger kind: the control plane stamps human.ask and code.run (a scheduler pass binds the produced artifact to the firing's marker and emits human.decision / code.result reaction events carrying it), so must-links chain through human decisions and code steps
deviations.reason: Review findings C1/C2: no bridge stamps human.ask or code.run, nothing emits human.decision, and no code.result trigger kind existed, so lineage broke at pr-upkeep's readiness -> human-merges-pr -> finish must-links. Owner approved option 1A on 2026-09-28, including the vocabulary change.

deviations.what: Sensitivity model (t30b): GitHub's audience is per repository (a public repo ranks public, a private repo org); exposure is approved per variable through a list on the declaration ('may this declaration expose data type V'), each entry approved by the variable's owner, replacing t30's per (declaration version, source version, variable, target) approval tasks
deviations.reason: Owner decision 2026-09-28 on decision 2: most repos, like this one, are public; a per-declaration exposure list is how the owner wants to approve exposure.

deviations.what: Break-glass stop powers (t19b): a break-glass credential bound to a human may deactivate a declaration and flip the engine switch to 'before', nothing else on the declaration routes; ADR 0014 section 3's break-glass clause is narrowed to that
deviations.reason: Owner decision 2026-09-28 on decision 4, for now, revisit if needed: an emergency needs a way to stop, not to create or activate; cortex found the clause unreachable (break-glass lacks the namespace-admin role).

deviations.what: Event mapping and start nodes (t38d): adopt t38's payload convention (payload.node, payload.origin {marker, artifact_kind, artifact_id, author, bridge_account}) as recorded design; an event without a verified marker always arrives at root; a declaration may declare start_from: any, or start_from by engine-derived node type ({host: spark|thor|orin}, {actor_kind: claude|codex|qwen|human|code}), recorded on each landing node from the action that produced it
deviations.reason: Owner decision 2026-09-28 on decision 3: option A plus declarations that can start from any node or from nodes of a type; types are derived from the action, not author labels.

deviations.what: Three trigger kinds join the closed vocabulary (t31b): pr-upkeep.pr (the live sweep fact, unrenamed), agent.result (a completed agent.work run's outcome, a proposed claim never evidence; agent.work also produces agent_work), jira.issue.transitioned (the neutral reaction to jira.transition). agent.result and jira.issue.transitioned have no emitter yet; t38d adds them.
deviations.reason: t31's migrated declarations could not chain with the registered kinds: no trigger carried a completed agent run's outcome, the live pr-upkeep entry fact had no kind, and the jira transition reaction had only legacy per-status names. Owner approved 2026-09-28.

deviations.what: The notifier becomes declarations: each notification case is a trigger-condition-action declaration posting through company/notify-discord (new reserved fact human.requested; discord.post contracts declare the bridge's sent/delivery_failed outcomes); muting a notification = deactivating its declaration; the nodes-notifier daemon stays only for graph runs until t37 (t41, in progress)
deviations.reason: Owner direction 2026-09-28 after the five-minute sweep flooded Discord: 'The notifier should be a Declaration as well. And then each case it fires - a TCA declaration.' The TCA inventory already listed the notifier as pending migration (docs/migration/tca-inventory.md).

deviations.what: Web inbox shows what is being decided and where (API resolved_context: each context ref resolved server-side; card leads with the question, PR/ticket/file links, finding, fix summary or blocked reason; audit collapsed), and filters into tabs Open (default: pending, deadline not passed) / Waiting (pending past deadline) / Decided (t43, t44, #332)
deviations.reason: Owner could not decide an approval in the inbox ('missing information', 'not a link, not clear where and what') and asked for filtering: 'by default show only what's open', with tabs for waiting and decided. Found while deciding live-test tasks.

deviations.reason: Live test: the sensitivity inbox was served a stale edge copy and whoami was edge-cached for ~1h (per-principal responses shared across Access users). Owner approved applying the rule ('Please do').

deviations.what: GitHub App nodes-culture-dev (App ID 5109433, installation 165818005, all agentculture repos; contents/PR/issues write, checks/statuses/actions read, no workflows/admin) replaces per-account PATs; token minting and webhook wiring are follow-up work on #331
deviations.reason: Live test: culture-claude's GITHUB_TOKEN_WORKER returned 401, blocking every agent GitHub write (chain 6-8). The owner created and installed the app and stored its key in grant; verified live (JWT -> /app, installation token with the declared permissions).

deviations.what: Agent actions offer a conventional 'blocked' outcome (output requires reason; a declaration may not define its own), emitted as agent.result; pr-upkeep and jira-intake gain blocked-*/close-blocked-* declarations that ask group/platform-maintainers with the agent's report (t40e; engine side lives in d2's t38 wiring)
deviations.reason: Live test chain 6: company/developer honestly reported it could not do the job (GitHub token 401), but stamp-pr's contract offered only 'stamped', so the attempt was contract_rejected, no agent.result was emitted and the chain went silent. Owner decision 2026-09-28: add blocked as suggested plus pr-upkeep routes.

deviations.what: A redelivered event never re-evaluates a declaration it already decided: Handle reads the event's evaluation trail once and skips decided (event, declaration) pairs across versions; progress-only pairs still resume (crash recovery); recorded failures are decided, a retry is a new event (t40a)
deviations.reason: Live in 'after': the sweep re-posts open Jira issues every tick and declhook passes duplicates through, so six events were re-evaluated every 5 minutes forever, a sensitivity-blocked firing silently retried, and a newly activated version could fire on an old event.

deviations.what: Sensitivity inbox responses are Cache-Control: no-store and a decided task refuses a blind second decision (409); changing a standing answer names the decision it supersedes (t40b)
deviations.reason: Live test: the pending list came from a stale edge copy and a second 'approved' was appended to an already-approved task.

deviations.what: The nodes CLI sends User-Agent culture-nodes/<version> (t40c)
deviations.reason: Cloudflare answers urllib's default Python-urllib agent with 403 (error 1010) in front of nodes.culture.dev, so every CLI call through Access failed.

deviations.what: Sweep cutover: 'timer' is a reserved name only FireSchedule may assert (timer rows forced to the schedule:<row> emitter); scheduler, worker, expire-approvals and human-fanout graph engines are drain-gated; grant-check.sh covers activated declarations' environmentRefs; production now sweeps through the pr-upkeep-sweep declaration on a 'timer' schedule row, the graph row disabled (t40d)
deviations.reason: Live: the 5-minute schedule emitted pr-upkeep.sweep.due, so the migrated timer-triggered sweep declaration never fired; the graph sweep kept running only because those engines lacked the drain gate. Design from the qwen cortex review.

deviations.what: Every bridge accepts a structured final answer that ends the text (bare JSON, fenced json, or prose followed by a JSON object with a string outcome) via a byte-identical final_answer.py; the conformance fake answers in the production shape (t40g)
